messages:
Mira Chen: ran regional bin-pack + kernel sweep across EU/US for L4/T4/A10G. Focus: embeddings (len=128) and small-chat (prompt ~120 tok, gen up to 256). Uploads + plots: https://gcs.redwood-inference/internal/bench/1857654321/
Mira Chen: TL;DR: A10G wins raw latency and tail for chat, L4 gives best cost/throughput for embeddings at high batch, T4 ok for low-budget EU but higher p95 on chat. 4-bit quant increases throughput but small chat quality dropped ~1-2% on our evals.
Kai Patel: can you paste the p95/p50 and tokens/sec summary for each GPU/workload?
Mira Chen: quick paste: 
```
Embeddings (len=128) batch=1  p95 (ms): A10G 28  | L4 40  | T4 55
Embeddings (len=128) batch=32 throughput (qps): A10G 2100 | L4 1950 | T4 1350
Cost per 1M embeds (est infra only): A10G $38 | L4 $29 | T4 $22

Small-chat (prompt120 -> gen256) p95 (ms): A10G 420 | L4 560 | T4 890
Small-chat tokens/sec (inference-only): A10G 120 tok/s | L4 95 tok/s | T4 60 tok/s
Cost per 1M output tokens (est): A10G $6.8 | L4 $5.1 | T4 $3.9
```
Mira Chen: note cost numbers include estimated instance hourly + amortized kernel overhead, not network. We used reserved pricing for baseline.
Ashley Gomez: which kernels gave the wins? any surprises for L4?
Mira Chen: notes: 
- A10G: fused_attn_v2 + packed-kv gave best p95 on chat (10-15% vs baseline).
- L4: cutlass fp16 gemm + mha_fused_light performed best when combined with continuous batching; L4 showed better steady-state throughput at batch>=8.
- T4: older cuBLAS paths were stable but higher variance; int8 paths exist but we saw quality drop unless calibration is tightened.
Mira Chen: command we ran (simplified):
```
./run_bench --model redwood-12b --gpu A10G --region us-west1 --workloads embeddings,chat --batches 1,8,32 --quant 16,8,4 --kernels fused_attn_v2,cutlass,mha_fused_light
```
Rajesh Iyer: QoS question — for Dedicated sizing, how many L4s per 100 qps of chat (SLO p95 < 600ms)?
Mira Chen: rough rule: for our chat profile (prompt120/gen256) 1 L4 (48GB) supports ~120 qps with batching & prefix cache. To hit p95 <600ms for 100 qps allow 1 box + 20% buffer (so 1.2 units) or reserve 2 for headroom and can handle spikes. A10G can get ~200 qps per instance.
Kai Patel: any notable regional differences?
Mira Chen: EU region had ~8-12% higher p95 on T4s vs US (thermal throttling + older infra in our lab racks). A10G differences were <3%.
Ashley Gomez: you said 4-bit regressed quality — do we have eval deltas?
Mira Chen: yes, on our internal conv-turn-level eval (mix of safety + utility) 8-bit fp16->int4 reduced coh/answer accuracy by ~1.5% absolute; 8-bit quant (qint8) was <0.5% delta. For embeddings int4 produced tiny embedding drift (cos sim drop ~0.7%) — acceptable for many use cases but flagged for search-recall sensitive apps.
bench-bot: uploaded plots: https://gcs.redwood-inference/internal/bench/1857654321/plots.tar.gz (sha256: a3f2...)
Kai Patel: awesome. can you add a short note for product about recommended defaults per workload?
Mira Chen: will do — draft: 1) embeddings: default L4 with batch=8-32 and int8-path if latency tolerant; 2) small-chat low-latency: A10G fp16 + fused_attn_v2; 3) cost-sensitive chat: L4 fp16 with continuous batching + prefix cache; 4) T4: fallback tier for non-critical workloads in EU. I'll drop into the PR for docs. :+1:
Rajesh Iyer: thanks — let's retest with canary quant params next week (tighter calib + mixed-precision).
Mira Chen: noted, scheduling a micro-sweep Mon morning and will post results.
